fields.Core Themes JSON: [{"title":"Seven Years In A Wheelchair","body":"Gillmore recounts a car accident and then a fall in 2003 that left her with a neurological disorder, extreme pain and years in a wheelchair. She describes trying nerve ablations, infusions and injections, then reaching outward to diets, detoxes, fasts, supplements, meditation, affirmations and binaural beats, and finding that none of it touched what she was living with. What stayed with her, she says, was noticing that her nerves would recover after a procedure while the underlying injury did not, and hearing doctors repeat that there was nothing more they could do for her."},{"title":"The Study That Sent Her Home","body":"She describes arriving at a medical study at a top hospital certain she was there to get her life back, wheeled in by a friend, set up on a gurney and connected to IVs, only to have the doctor review her chart and tell her she could not take part because they did not expect her to improve. She recounts arguing that this was her life, being treated outside the study anyway, and going home to no change. Lying there afterward, she says, a question about the placebo surfaced in her head and gave her a reason not to quit."},{"title":"Different Personalities, Different Illnesses","body":"The research that jolted her, Gillmore says, involved people with multiple personality disorder, including a reported case of a woman described as medically blind in some personalities and sighted in others, and cases where one personality carried an illness while another did not. That pushed her question away from whether trauma existed and toward why it seemed to land so unevenly, since she had noticed police and military people who had been through extreme events without becoming ill. Her working frame became ingredients, a specific combination rather than trauma on its own, and belief alone was not enough."},{"title":"The Guilt Underneath The Trauma","body":"The counterintuitive piece in her own case, Gillmore recounts, was survivors guilt. Working an early morning shift in California, she had been on the phone with colleagues in the trade towers on 9/11, could do nothing as it unfolded, then watched the footage replay for months and carried a suppressed sense that she should have died saving others. She traces the feeling back further, to a moment around age four when another child said they would die for their family and she concluded her own answer made her selfish. Clearing the trauma, she says, did not clear the guilt."},{"title":"Tuning Forks And Repeating Patterns","body":"Garton sets his own practice alongside hers, describing biofield tuning, where forks are used to find stuck energy around the body and, he says, often prompt spontaneous recall of an old memory. He recounts a visiting relative with decades of back pain and a conversation about losing his father's support, and his own stubborn shoulder injury, after which his first marriage ended and he recognized the story he had been living, that enduring poor treatment made him the good guy. Both talk about symptoms as a kind of check engine light, and Gillmore insists the change was the gift, not the injury."}]
fields.Intro Paragraph 1: Can the mind really heal the body? In this episode of the InnerVerse Podcast, we sit down with Brandy Gillmore, who spent seven years in a wheelchair due to "incurable" chronic pain before discovering the missing link in her recovery. Tune in for Brandy’s journey from network engineering to mind-body healing, exploring the specific subconscious ingredients, like hidden survivors' guilt, that can trap the body in a state of illness even when you’re doing everything else right.

fields.Plus Core Themes JSON: [{"title": "Self Sacrifice as a Cultural Program", "body": "Chance names the thing he calls the MESSOP, the way a guilt heavy Baptist upbringing teaches that the best person in the room is the one who sacrifices himself for everybody else, and he points out that if everyone lives that way, everyone ends up sacrificed. Brandy recognizes it immediately, because she grew up looking at a crucifix two stories tall and had already decided that feeling guilty was what proved she had a conscience. She held onto guilt for everything under the sun while believing she was perfectly happy, which is exactly how a pattern hides."}, {"title": "Light Carries Information Between Living Things", "body": "The conversation goes back down the biophoton rabbit hole with the studies Brandy collected. A cut apple emits more light than an uncut one. Anger raises emissions, but so do cancer cells, which is why she distrusts the advice to simply raise your vibration. People with type two diabetes show increased emission from the forehead and less from the torso. Participants imagining white light lit up on the right side of the head and not the left. Most striking are the egg studies, where light from one egg could speed repair in another or slow it down."}, {"title": "The Emotional Shift Nobody Measures", "body": "On a panel of doctors, one told the room about women whose tissue stopped growing cancerous cells in a dish after a month of eating well and exercising, offering it as proof that mindset was irrelevant. Brandy asked what it does to a woman to be given permission to spend a month on herself without guilt, and the audience answered for her. She applies the same lens to the Lyme story Chance tells about fixing light exposure, and to people who go vegan, feel like a good person, and credit the food."}, {"title": "How Owies and Disasters Get Linked", "body": "Chance admits the kissing the booboo idea landed hard, since he and his wife are already coaching grandparents away from the anxious response, and he wonders whether praise for getting hurt is any safer. Brandy answers with a natural disaster. Two people live through the same event, and one loses community while the other finds it for the first time, so the same experience wires opposite meanings. That is why a pattern can be intermittent, why a person can feel successful and sympathetic at once, and why nobody who ever got a kiss on a scrape is doomed."}, {"title": "Universal Wi-Fi and the Ethics of Receiving", "body": "Brandy describes the ability she developed after healing, comparing it to mirror touch synesthesia and to clearing a restaurant so you can hear the whisper across the room. Rather than silencing the mind, she shut off the stations that were errors. Chance recognizes the same thing in his own work, down to his ears popping when he finds a signal, and argues that conscience is the everyday version of it. Both agree the gate is integrity, that you have to ask before anything answers, and that you can set terms with your own body."}]

fields.Plus Quotes JSON: [{"text": "If we all sacrifice ourselves for everyone, everybody got sacrificed.", "author": "Chance Garton", "portrait": "https://images.squarespace-cdn.com/content/5987d897cf81e0278ec5322e/a784fd99-3e6f-436c-a8f3-c4f913b855ed/profile-pic.jpg?content-type=image%2Fjpeg"}, {"text": "I discovered a lot of amazing things that are incredible, and whatever other people discover, the integrity thing to do is make sure to give them credit for what they discovered.", "author": "Brandy Gillmore", "portrait": "https://images.squarespace-cdn.com/content/5987d897cf81e0278ec5322e/e3e7cc7c-667f-4f30-aaba-68e590aa771a/BRANDY-GILMORE.jpg?content-type=image%2Fjpeg"}, {"text": "When you go down the rabbit hole of energy influencing energy, it becomes a little bit mind-boggling.", "author": "Brandy Gillmore", "portrait": "https://images.squarespace-cdn.com/content/5987d897cf81e0278ec5322e/e3e7cc7c-667f-4f30-aaba-68e590aa771a/BRANDY-GILMORE.jpg?content-type=image%2Fjpeg"}, {"text": "Universe, God, divine energy, mother nature, whatever you want to call it, made us really freaking amazing beings, and it's incredible.", "author": "Brandy Gillmore", "portrait": "https://images.squarespace-cdn.com/content/5987d897cf81e0278ec5322e/e3e7cc7c-667f-4f30-aaba-68e590aa771a/BRANDY-GILMORE.jpg?content-type=image%2Fjpeg"}, {"text": "How many of us grew up burying our emotions anyway?", "author": "Brandy Gillmore", "portrait": "https://images.squarespace-cdn.com/content/5987d897cf81e0278ec5322e/e3e7cc7c-667f-4f30-aaba-68e590aa771a/BRANDY-GILMORE.jpg?content-type=image%2Fjpeg"}, {"text": "So often people look at patterns, and they say, \"Well, it can't be my pattern because it's not everywhere in my life, so you're the problem. I'm the good one, you're the bad one.\"", "author": "Brandy Gillmore", "portrait": "https://images.squarespace-cdn.com/content/5987d897cf81e0278ec5322e/e3e7cc7c-667f-4f30-aaba-68e590aa771a/BRANDY-GILMORE.jpg?content-type=image%2Fjpeg"}, {"text": "The innate knowing to just know something and trust that you know it is a faculty everyone has to a degree whether or not they realize because everyone has a conscience.", "author": "Chance Garton", "portrait": "https://images.squarespace-cdn.com/content/5987d897cf81e0278ec5322e/a784fd99-3e6f-436c-a8f3-c4f913b855ed/profile-pic.jpg?content-type=image%2Fjpeg"}, {"text": "A lot of times, positive thinking, while it's well-intentioned, can be trying to just amp up what's in the now without really addressing what's underneath also.", "author": "Brandy Gillmore", "portrait": "https://images.squarespace-cdn.com/content/5987d897cf81e0278ec5322e/e3e7cc7c-667f-4f30-aaba-68e590aa771a/BRANDY-GILMORE.jpg?content-type=image%2Fjpeg"}, {"text": "The first step in the whole process is you got to ask that part of self or ask the universal Wi-Fi for the guidance or ask the question.", "author": "Chance Garton", "portrait": "https://images.squarespace-cdn.com/content/5987d897cf81e0278ec5322e/a784fd99-3e6f-436c-a8f3-c4f913b855ed/profile-pic.jpg?content-type=image%2Fjpeg"}, {"text": "You can adjust the parameters of how this interaction occurs, and you should be mindful of that, because otherwise you could be taking on stuff you don't want to take on.", "author": "Chance Garton", "portrait": "https://images.squarespace-cdn.com/content/5987d897cf81e0278ec5322e/a784fd99-3e6f-436c-a8f3-c4f913b855ed/profile-pic.jpg?content-type=image%2Fjpeg"}]
